item.title: SCP Idea: "Albularyo"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: YES

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The basic SCP article layout.

Elevator Pitch:

  • Nato Caluag is an "albularyo", roughly translates to "witch doctor" in english who can conjure instances of "Engkantos" a Filipino mythological creature capable of applying a "sumpa" or curse.
  • This SCP is contained in a cell where he cannot have access to any object that could possibly have been marked with someone's DNA or even fingerprint. A microphone hidden from this SCP's sight must always be present inside his cell.
  • Moreover, any form of media that could potentially contain piece of a person's identity can never be shown to this SCP.
  • As long as this Albularyo sees a person of interest, obtain a piece of their DNA or even acquire an object with that person's fingerprint, if this SCP is in a hostile mood, he will have a "conversation" with an "Engkanto" who he claims to be his best friend and command it to lay a "sumpa" on the chosen victim. (This is why the microphone is necessary, because he verbally converses out loud.)
  • The random victim will experience immense pain on random parts of the body (chosen by Nato) and orifices of the victim will slowly discharge tadpoles and prematurely born insects.
  • Victims of this SCP can never die from the curse. However, the "sumpa" is able to be cured. Just not in a medical sense.
  • Scientific way of cure like medicine or surgery can NEVER prevent the "sumpa". BUT the only way to cure it is to take the victim to another "albularyo" who can perform the ritual of curse-removal.
  • To avoid this hostile activity, a full rosary and the "divine mercy" ritual must sincerely be recited every 3 in the afternoon. (Priests are usually called to perform the procedure and applied with memetics after)

Central Narrative:
Nato Caluag was considered a vengeful and hateful albularyo. Coincidentally, he was also a powerful one. Able to easily conjure Engkantos (who were actually the enemies of the witch doctors).
In the provinces of The Philippines, albularyos are considered healers and able to remove curses from victims. But Nato was the opposite of this and would apply the curse with the help of his "friend", an "Engkanto" that he met when he was young.
Nato grabbed the attention of the foundation after consecutive cases of unexplainable diseases were reported in the province of Bulacan.
Nato is actually the elder brother of Ed Caluag, a famous paranormal expert in Filipino mainstream media, but when the foundation took him, memetics were given to Ed and his family, completely forgetting his existence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • Explores the pseudo-science belief of Filipino culture, especially the "albularyos" and "engkantos" with a unique take
  • This SCP can talk to engkantos and demand them to apply a curse ("sumpa") on a human, but this will never kill them, only make them suffer. And the only way to cure the curse is to find another albularyo capable of removing the curse.
  • Affiliation with a famous Filipino icon, but since he was taken by the foundation, his existence is not known to the public.

Additional Notes:

  • I'd gladly accept your critique on this and what should be improved.
  • I'd just like to know whether this idea is similar to an already-existing SCP or even tale?

I have the same problem with this that I do with a lot of "[religious, folk lore, or pop cultural thing] is back, in SCP format" articles. Namely, that much of the enjoyment and understanding that is derived from the specific ways in which the story is told and uses its medium. Stripped of the specific story-telling context, and not adapted to the medium of a SCP document, it loses almost all of its value as anything but a reference. Just as I wouldn't be interested in reading The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, The SCP Article, I wasn't particularly interested in reading this.

I will say that I enjoyed the dreamy quality of the recovered footage, but the article overall did little to nothing for me.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) Again, you guys do things weird here. Most people aren't used to the whole "edit the original document every time a change is made"; it's normally assumed you would read the entire thread. Even a bullpen would consider every detail and then make changes; making piecemeal corrections tends to dilute the overall product.

Something that takes getting used to. Note that the original statement has yet again been edited.

2) By the same token, there are only so many details that you can put into 400 words, and I've seen that limit enforced for even going a few words over (I'm currently at 395, in case you're curious). Note carefully that I'm not arguing for a greater word count or that I don't see a reason for that limitation (even seeing as few abuses as I have of that here, it's hard not to see the wisdom therein), just saying that if you put a limit you need to make allowances for it.

As a writer. you just can't always make allowances for every sniggling detail, and sometimes you need to make a decision between making a complicated concept clear and delineating the relationship with The Foundation; which would you prefer as a reviewer?

Yeah, it's a jerk point, but if you want the best possible SCPs you need to make allowances that you may be missing some information you see as mandatory in order to better elaborate other information.

What's hardest about speculating what 447 does to dead bodies is NOT wondering just how horrible it is, but how it is just NOT-horrible enough that researchers have considered marketing it for funding (and may have already done so with the green milk). After all, a certain anartist dumped a ton of 447 onto his art that is a mountainous pile of dead bodies, yet this event was possible to cover up. And we have seen plenty of horrible things uncensored in this website, so what makes this worthy of expunging? And research into it may result in termination.

Mmm… how about 447 with a dead body makes all knowledge relating to body antimemetic? Including the person's life and death, and the contact with 447 itself. Okay sure, maybe it's a lazy copout? But I don't see much contradicting it (Ofc, there must be some other explanations). It'd be okay for this self-containing event to happen very rarely in public, and the Foundation may want to keep it secret from even its employees, as 447 can wipe entire lifetimes worth of events from the public consciousness with almost no effort. The complete censoring of 447's effect on corpses on an already confidential document could seem conspicuous, if not for the O5's clear intended comment.

I could've kept this pointless comment to myself, but whatever, I'll post it. But I presume someone probably already had this exact same thought somewhere on reddit,discord,irc,idk, let's be honest.

item.title: A very long story about a spider and three goons
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama action

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: A single spider causes all genetic brain diseases. One woman wants to kill it for taking away her daughter, one man wants to protect it because he wants it to be studied, one girl just wants to be at peace and to succumb to it. An exploration in two layers. On one level, The Chaos Insurgency and what it stands for. On another, loss and how we respond to it.

Central Narrative: Two doctors are employed by The Foundation to research the source of all memory loss and neurodegenerative disease, a big spider. Elizabeth, loses her daughter to a brain disease. Kenneth sees The Foundation using the SCP as a weapon. Elizabeth and Kenneth defect from The Foundation to join the Chaos Insurgency. Now free from direct oversight, Elizabeth decides to kill the spider in revenge. Kenneth wants to capture and study the spider, wanting to prevent The Foundation or other groups from utilizing it for their own ends. Jacquelyn, a student of Elizabeth who was left with The Foundation when Liz defected, half-heartedly pursues the insurgents because she wants to speak with Elizabeth.

What each character represents:
Elizabeth:
- The Insurgency that wants to make the world better with anomalies.
- A self-destructive spite toward the thing that took away her daughter.
- Wins in the end. Destroys the SCP, ridding the world of the force that killed her daughter. To her, the SCP doesn't simply represent neurological diseases. Instead, to Elizabeth - and the audience - it's a stand-in for death.

Kenneth:
- The Insurgency that's simply trying to be a better version of The Foundation.
- A belief that death, even tragic death, is a part of life and should be accepted.
- Ultimately betrayed by Elizabeth and killed while attempting to stop her.

Jacquelyn:
- Simple apathy. The victim of the story, abandoned by Elizabeth and caught in the crossfire.
- Has an opportunity to stop Elizabeth. Doesn't, choosing to simply euthanise herself with happy memories excreted by the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: need help with this one

Additional Notes: Might be too melodramatic of a plot.

item.title: Re: The Shield that Redirects its Damage
item.content:encoded:
Hello HelloThere! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A viking shield that when held by a living person will cause a blue energy field to cover it. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). However, it does have its limits.

Overall, the skip feels like a "thing that does a thing", as the object doesn't seem to have much of purpose or origin. The main focus from both the narrative and concept seem to be the effects, which currently fall fairly flat, as there isn't anything beyond "shield that deflects attacks". What about this will make me as the reader invested? is there any sort of history behind the skip? whats its purpose? how do its effects relate to that purpose?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The shield was discovered in Norway in a viking ship burial by some archaeologists. The SCP came to the foundation's attention when reports of a cursed and powerful shield erupted upon its discovery so an investigation was initiated and the SCP was recovered. Tests and experiments were conducted to understand how it works which usually consisted of D-Class personnel and weaponized machinery attacking it.

While there is a setup here, a strong middle act and payoff are missing. The story isn't building up to anything, or showing much other than "Foundation finds and then tests something". The tests alone won't be able to carry the story, as they don't offer anything to really get invested in.

Along with this the narrative is missing a conflict. All of the events go off without a hitch and the Foundation doesn't have any sort of reason of care about the skip, which makes the story feel a bit flat and unnatural.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is unknown where the shield gained its anomalous ability and who the creator/original wielder was. There is also little information on how the SCP generates its blue energy field though it is possible that there is some sort of mystical or magical force surrounding it.

This feels like a quick/lazy way to explain the skips effects and origin, especially with the lack of other main focuses (the Foundation is only testing the skips effects) in the narrative or concept.

The shield could provide potential use to the foundation, but if fallen into the wrong hands it could lead to many problems.

I would recommend you look at making this more apparent in the narrative (from what I can see this barely gets mention in the story). Show how this would be useful, why it's dangerous in the wrong hands, what would happen ect.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Recommendations:
-My main issue is the lack of a strong conflict and payoff in the narrative, there isn't much to really get invested in. - I would recommend expanding upon possible ideas for conflict or exploitation. (the Foundation using it for their own gain, other parties trying to steal it, ect.)

-the skip itself only really shows its effects, which alone aren't interesting enough to carry the article. - I wold recommend you get a rough idea of the origin and purpose of the skip, as developing it fully, will allow you to pick and choose what is and isn't necessary to include. (it can also help with developing the narrative!)

- the plot line feels unfinished due to the lack of a strong payoff. - Show something more than just tests, what does everything build up to? why are they testing it? what is learnt by the end? ect.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

item.title: Ever Upwards
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Existential thriller, mystery

Elevator Pitch:
+ Elevator Pitch
- Elevator Pitch

This scp is, in a sense, humanity's seeming desire to leave earth's atmosphere and explore outer space. This scp was discovered once the foundation began to notice strange patterns in the direction and movement of every human and manmade object launched into space, as well as every other object in space (planets, stars, etc), which all appear to be converging to an unknown spot in spacetime at irregular speeds.

Central Narrative:
+ Central Narrative
- Central Narrative

While investigating several other space related anomalies, the foundation begins to put together a strange pattern in the movement of every object that has been launched into space, which all eventually begin to travel in the same exact direction. Digging further, they find a cut section of the Apollo 11 landing, during which mike collins seems to jump and be dragged out in this exact same direction for a few seconds, contrary to the observed gravitational effects of the moon. Curiously, satelites in orbit around earth such as the ISS are unaffected, as well as celestial bodies such as the planets, moons, and sun. However, calculations run by the foundation indicate that these bodies only appear to be unaffected, and have actually been moving in an even pace to one another in this direction for a while. Finally, the foundation uncovers that, over the course of millenia, every object in the universe has been traveling towards a single undefined point in space.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ Hook/Attention Grabber
- Hook/Attention Grabber

After running some tests, the foundation manages to calculate the coordinates for this point. After a predictably long journey, they finally manage to send a ship to the coordinates, which finds a barely describable fold in spacetime where all things are seemingly erased. Ordered to return, the unmanned ship curiously defies its controls and moves towards the fold, and strong radio interference is heard as the ship displays a white void. The foundation finds the sounds to be their only lead, and work to decipher a potential meaning. Although they fail, an incident occurs where these sounds are heard again from the sky, this time being mysteriously comprehensible, with the message:
"You have protected your world
from a great many threats,
from those which are incomprehensible,
and for that I am proud.
But what comes now you are not prepared for,
nor am I,
so I must protect you now,
within my unwavering.
Join me,
In this void,
and travel ever upward,
for you have no other choice"

The article ends with a question: If after all the foundation has fought, this void only interferes now, then what exactly is coming for us?

Additional Notes: Hope this isn't too similar to anything else and that it's interesting!

item.title: Individual Rating Modules for Log Entries
item.content:encoded:
Low-quality content naturally piles up in places like 682's termination log, 1459's extended logs, and other very large collaborative lists. Inevitably, a page curator has to go through and prune away the bad entries. I imagine that this is tiresome and time-consuming for the curator, and it also means that garbage entries in these logs live much longer than an equally garbage SCP would. If there were some way to install individual rating modules for each item on the log, so they could be voted on individually, then perhaps that might save some time for the curator and shorten the lifespan of the bad entries.

I thought that the log of extranormal events or unexplained locations was already like this, but it seems that I was mistaken.

item.title: Seeking Critique (Love Potion No. 9)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: This is an SCP based upon the narrative created by the song, Love Potion No. 9, made popular by The Clovers in 1959. The premise is that the SCP is the actual love potion described in the song, more or less. The object itself is a safe object, characterized as being an opaque black liquid contained within a small glass bottle. The liquid itself is described as smelling of turpentine. Its anomalous property is that it causes the drinker to lose all romantic and sexual discretion, except for a marked increase in the attractiveness of members of law enforcement.

Central Narrative: This object came to the attention of the Foundation after a young man was arrested and brought to a mental asylum after falling under the effects of the love potion and succeeding in his attempt to passionately kiss a police officer on patrol. The young man informed officials that he was compelled to behave in that manner after drinking a potion, created by a gypsy fortune teller named Madame Ruth in order to cure him of his bad luck with women.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This is an SCP based on a well known piece of pop culture history. I feel like people will find it quite amusing and maybe even humorous.

Additional Notes: I hope you guys see this as a lighthearted, humorous attempt at an SCP article.

item.content:encoded:
The following logs have been pruned from the log:

+ Pruned logs
– hide block

Unexplained Location UE-655588
Description: A small communal, Christian church marked in city records as "the West Tennesse Peoples Church of Churchism", shown to be entirely constructed of organic matter. The only other feature of note surrounding UE-655588 is that the object was formerly Pastor Henry Ecclesia, who slowly transformed into the church between 1970 and 1971.
Date of Containment: 1971-03-12
Location: Outside Clarksville, Tennesse.
Security Protocol: The church is to be patrolled by two guards, under the cover story of Asbestos Cleanup operations. All individuals who enter the church are to be removed. Any individuals who discover the objects anomalous properties are to be provided with Class-A amnestics.
Note: A small plaque was found engraved on the southwestern flank of the structure, transcribed below:

TO THE GLORY OF GOD 1971:

THIS CHURCH WAS MADE OF AND BY PASTOR HENRY ECCLESIA. HIS SACRIFICE TO BECOME ONE WITH THE LORD AND HIS FOLLOWERS WILL NEVER BE FORGOTTEN. HIS BLOOD, SWEAT, TEARS, ORGANS, SKIN, AND MUSCLES WERE USED TO BUILD A HOME FOR OUR LORD AND HIS SUN. [sic]

”Those who wish to be a church can be under God, for that is his way.” - Jesus Christ (Assumed).

Unexplained Location UE-96843
Description: A small Victorian Era house originally owned by 'Sir Oswald Francis', a tea-trader from the United Kingdom. When the attic door is opened, it will lead to an extradimensional location roughly resembling a massive tea plantation. In the centre of the plantation is a large factory complex. Every individual who enters the pocket dimension will simultaneously appear in both the attic entrance (which leads to a small shack) and the factory. They will also feel an impossible compulsion to harvest tea from the plantation and put the leaves on a pully within the structure, and then to place a weight on the other pully. The individual who moves out of the factory will be unable to exit the dimension, whereas the individuals who enter via the attic entrance will be able to exit. Several notable individuals are within the structure including, but not limited to, George Washington, Winston Churchill, Queen Elizabeth II, Sir Oswald Francis, Kristina Francis, every member of the beetles, and 83 duplicates of an unidentified worker.
Date of Containment: Since Foundation Inception.
Location: Ganges Delta, Bangladesh.
Security Protocol: Two guards stationed around the structure. Produced tea checked for anomalies and sold as a part of Sir Conrod Products (an SCP foundation front company.)

Unexplained Location UE-39221
Description: Roughly 204 billion exoplanets 189 billion light-years from Earth, with several anomalous effects. The planets exist within the radius of each other where gravitational action would result in their destruction, and move in erratic and impossible patterns. The planets, when viewed through a satellite, resemble 21 tangled double-helix structures forming into large structures. Despite these structures large mass, no gravitational effects occur on nearby planets. The double helix structure of this planetary system is sometimes threaded through large masses of planets, which somehow causes a single helix structure to move from this mass, flip, and then thread itself together with another double helix structure.
When the atmospheric composition and sizes of these planets are accounted for, the planets can be assigned to several elements from the periodic table. Using this model, the planetary structure has been found to be an exact match to the genome of a human male, with 16% Irish heritage, 53% Indian heritage, 30.2% English descent and 0.2% from other locations. The individual is known to have blue eyes, red hair, and pale white skin. So far no exact genetic match for this has been found.

Date of Containment: 2014-05-12, After discovery by foundation FTL probe.
Location: Galaxy supercluster XY-539222.
Security Protocol: It is unlikely that UE-39221 will ever be discovered, due to extreme distances from the earth, and as such, no security protocol is needed.

All of these logs were pruned for length — entries to this list should be of relatively short length, and not extensively detailed.

You did a really good job putting personality in all of the characters. I Loved the jokes and the dialogue as well. Easy +1.

I only have two critiques, but they're minor (get it). First is a grammatical error. In the first part of addendum 1, you wrote "D-060173 was tethered and given an heat-proof armor, oxygen tank, and night-vision goggles." It should be "D-060173 was tethered and given an heat-proof armor, an oxygen tank, and night-vision goggles."

Secondly is that at the end of the description, you included the sentence "The exact nature of SCP-5594 is unknown and an investigation is ongoing". I don't think that sentence makes much sense for two reasons. Firstly, that paragraph was pretty specific in describing the effects and entities of the scp, so it felt weird for you to say it wasn't fully understood. In the context of the article as a whole it makes even less sense, since there isn't exactly any mystery as to what's going on by the end.

Other than that, it was a very fun read
